text:
anya: heads up, compliance requested a stricter retention class for kernel traces. current forensic-retain=180d, they want 365d for kernel panics. implications?
pager-bot: compliance ticket COMP-1010 created.
michael-sre: longer retention increases S3 costs and KMS key lifecycle management. also affects egress when sharing for triage. we should tier: keep full traces 365d in forensic-retain, keep a scrubbed summary in forensic-summary 365d, and allow JIT exports for vendors only after approval.
olga-legal: legal asks that any external debug shares have a legal-approved NDA attached and PII scrubbed. for high-risk customers, require signed DPA amendment.
anya: proposed policy text: "Kernel panic traces are retained 365 days in secure forensic storage (encrypt-at-rest with CMK). External sharing requires: sec-lead approval, privacy sign-off, scrubber report attached, and vendor NDA on file. JIT exports must be timeboxed and KMS-wrapped."
michael-sre: add requirement to rotate CMKs yearly and rewrap sensitive forensic objects during rotation window. add an audit tag 'trace-retain-365'.
anya: ok will draft PR to retention policy doc and add runbook changes. assigning: anya to PR, michael-sre to update runbook, olga-legal to prepare NDA template.
pager-bot: assignment updated.
olga-legal: quick note: also include a clause to require automatic masking of IP addresses for external deliveries unless customer permits.
anya: noted. I will include IP masking and the scrubber config examples in the PR.
michael-sre: leaving action: michael-sre to calculate storage delta and add to the budget forecast.
anya: thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
